title: Osimertinib in Untreated EGFR-Mutated Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (FLAURA)
sections: Design

FLAURA was a double blind phase 3 trial in 556 people with previously untreated advanced NSCLC carrying an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation, randomised to osimertinib or to a standard EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (gefitinib or erlotinib).
Results

Median progression free survival was 18.9 months with osimertinib and 10.2 months with gefitinib or erlotinib (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.46). Objective response rates were similar at 80% and 76%. Grade 3 or higher adverse events were less frequent with osimertinib (34%) than with the comparator (45%).
Conclusion
First line osimertinib gave longer progression free survival than earlier generation EGFR TKIs with a lower rate of serious adverse events, and underpins NICE TA654.

title: Osimertinib in Resected EGFR-Mutated Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (ADAURA)
sections: Design

ADAURA was a double blind phase 3 trial of adjuvant osimertinib against placebo for up to 3 years in 682 people with completely resected stage IB to IIIA NSCLC carrying an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation; previous adjuvant chemotherapy was allowed.
Results

In stage II to IIIA disease, disease free survival at 24 months was 90% with osimertinib and 44% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.17). In the overall stage IB to IIIA population the hazard ratio for disease recurrence or death was 0.20, and the hazard ratio for central nervous system recurrence or death was 0.18.
Conclusion
Adjuvant osimertinib substantially reduced recurrence after resection of EGFR mutated NSCLC and underpins NICE TA1043, which stops treatment at 3 years.

title: Pembrolizumab versus Chemotherapy for PD-L1-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (KEYNOTE-024)
sections: Design

KEYNOTE-024 randomised 305 people with untreated advanced NSCLC, PD-L1 expression on at least 50% of tumour cells and no EGFR mutation or ALK translocation to pembrolizumab or investigator choice platinum based chemotherapy.
Results

Median progression free survival was 10.3 months with pembrolizumab and 6.0 months with chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.50). Overall survival was longer with pembrolizumab (hazard ratio for death 0.60), the response rate was 44.8% against 27.8%, and treatment related grade 3 to 5 adverse events occurred in 26.6% against 53.3%.
Conclusion
For PD-L1 high advanced NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations, first line pembrolizumab improved progression free and overall survival with fewer serious adverse events, and underpins NICE TA531.

title: Pembrolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Metastatic Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (KEYNOTE-189)
sections: Design

KEYNOTE-189 randomised 616 people with untreated metastatic non squamous NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations, in a 2 to 1 ratio, to pemetrexed and a platinum drug with pembrolizumab or with placebo, followed by pembrolizumab or placebo with pemetrexed maintenance.
Results

The estimated rate of overall survival at 12 months was 69.2% with pembrolizumab combination and 49.4% with placebo combination (hazard ratio for death 0.49). Median progression free survival was 8.8 months against 4.9 months (hazard ratio 0.52), and the overall survival benefit was seen in every PD-L1 category, including tumours with PD-L1 below 1%.
Conclusion
Adding pembrolizumab to pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy improved survival in non squamous NSCLC regardless of PD-L1 expression, and underpins NICE TA683.

title: Neoadjuvant Nivolumab plus Chemotherapy in Resectable Lung Cancer (CheckMate 816)
sections: Design
CheckMate 816 randomised 358 people with resectable stage IB to IIIA NSCLC to three cycles of nivolumab plus platinum based chemotherapy or platinum based chemotherapy alone before surgery.
Results

Median event free survival was 31.6 months with nivolumab plus chemotherapy and 20.8 months with chemotherapy alone (hazard ratio 0.63). The pathological complete response rate was 24.0% against 2.2%, and adding nivolumab did not increase adverse events or reduce the feasibility of surgery.
Conclusion
Neoadjuvant nivolumab with chemotherapy lengthened event free survival and increased pathological complete response, and underpins NICE TA876.

title: Adjuvant atezolizumab after adjuvant chemotherapy in resected stage IB to IIIA non-small-cell lung cancer (IMpower010)
sections: Design

IMpower010 enrolled 1280 people with completely resected stage IB to IIIA NSCLC; after up to four cycles of cisplatin based adjuvant chemotherapy, 1005 were randomised to 16 cycles of atezolizumab or best supportive care.
Results

Atezolizumab improved disease free survival in stage II to IIIA disease with PD-L1 expression on at least 1% of tumour cells (hazard ratio 0.66) and in all stage II to IIIA disease (hazard ratio 0.79); the benefit was concentrated in tumours with higher PD-L1 expression.
Conclusion
Adjuvant atezolizumab after chemotherapy is a treatment option for resected PD-L1 positive stage II to IIIA NSCLC, within the populations defined by NICE.

title: Alectinib in Resected ALK-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (ALINA)
sections: Design
ALINA randomised 257 people with completely resected ALK positive stage IB (tumour at least 4 cm) to IIIA NSCLC to adjuvant alectinib for 2 years or to four cycles of platinum based chemotherapy.
Results

In stage II to IIIA disease the disease free survival rate at 2 years was 93.8% with alectinib and 63.0% with chemotherapy (hazard ratio for disease recurrence or death 0.24), and alectinib also reduced central nervous system recurrence.
Conclusion
Adjuvant alectinib markedly improved disease free survival over chemotherapy in resected ALK positive NSCLC and underpins NICE TA1014.

title: Sotorasib for Lung Cancers with KRAS p.G12C Mutation (CodeBreaK 100)
sections: Design

CodeBreaK 100 was a single group phase 2 trial of sotorasib in 126 people with KRAS G12C mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after earlier standard treatment, most of whom had received both platinum chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
Results
An objective response occurred in 37.1% of patients, with a median duration of response of 11.1 months. Median progression free survival was 6.8 months and median overall survival was 12.5 months.
Conclusion
Sotorasib produced durable responses in previously treated KRAS G12C mutated NSCLC and underpins NICE TA781, which makes it available through the Cancer Drugs Fund.
